items.title: backlog spec: how should a comment stating a workflow SHAPE or prose ENUMERATION be mechanically checked?
items.eli5: Some source-code comments describe a workflow's shape (e.g. "steps run in this order") or enumerate a fixed list, without naming a specific file/symbol/path. The existing check:comment-code-citations gate (shipped 2026-10-04) only reconciles comments that name a concrete identifier — a shape or enumeration names none, so it is never checked, and the code behind it can drift silently (the entry cites a 2026-08-31 continuityScore header as the motivating case). The backlog entry already states the desired end property, but not the mechanism: there is no existing tool that parses a free-form "shape" or "enumeration" claim and reconciles it against code. Turning this into a concrete, implementable spec (what counts as a checkable shape/enumeration claim, and what tool would check it) is a design call, not a mechanical fix leg 2 can apply on its own.
items.question: Should this stay an open backlog item as-is (no mechanism proposed yet), should it be narrowed to a scoped A→B spec (e.g. "require every workflow-shape comment to cite a sites-pinned test" rather than a general-purpose shape parser), or should it be dropped as not worth mechanizing (rely on doc review to catch drift here)?

options.label: Keep as-is
options.answer: Keep the entry open as currently written; no new mechanism proposed yet, revisit later.

options.label: Narrow to a sites-pinned-citation requirement
options.answer: Narrow the fix to requiring every workflow-shape/enumeration comment to cite a sites-pinned test or spec, rather than building a general shape/enumeration parser.

options.label: Drop — not worth mechanizing
options.answer: Drop this entry; rely on the nightly doc-review pass to catch workflow-shape/enumeration drift by hand rather than building a mechanical check.

evidence: docs/backlog/open-bugs.md:35-41 (current entry text, quoted in full in the subject).
check:comment-code-citations (shipped 2026-10-04 per the entry's own text) resolves backticked paths/symbols only; verified its guard-reach row lists this gap rather than covering it.

leg-2 mechanical triage sweep (2026-10-21, litellm/medium) independently classified this entry owner_decision_needed: "states a goal to mechanically reconcile prose workflow shapes and enumerations without specifying the design or mechanism."

premise_probes.contains: A code comment that states a workflow SHAPE or a prose ENUMERATION is checked by nothing

items.subject: The section header "Synthesis narrative (always runs)" says the synthesis-narrative obligation always emits host work, but its own body text and the code say the layer is optional and can resolve with zero host work emitted
items.title: spec/audit-workflow-design.md: fix or clarify the "Synthesis narrative (always runs)" header, which contradicts its own body and the code
items.eli5: spec/audit-workflow-design.md has a section titled "Synthesis narrative (always runs)". The very next sentences in that same section call the narrative layer "optional" and say a user can decline it with no host step ever emitted — and the actual code (src/audit/orchestrator/obligationPolicy.ts, the synthesis_narrative_current obligation) confirms this: when a session passes narrativeEnabled: false, the obligation resolves deterministically to OMIT with no host work at all. So the header's "always runs" is either (a) a documentation bug that should be reworded (e.g. "the obligation is always evaluated/reached in priority order" rather than "host work is always produced"), or (b) the header is deliberately using "always runs" to mean something narrower than "produces host work" and should stay as-is with a one-clause clarification added. Both the nightly reviewer and an independent adversary agent reviewed this file tonight; the adversary caught this specific tension and the reviewer did not flag it, so this is a judgment call about what the header was meant to say, not a confirmed one-line typo.
items.question: Should the header "## Synthesis narrative (always runs)" in spec/audit-workflow-design.md be reworded to match the optional/tri-state behavior the code and the rest of the section already state, or is the current header intentional (meaning something other than "host work is always produced") and should be left as-is?

options.label: Reword the header
options.answer: Reword "Synthesis narrative (always runs)" to reflect that the obligation is always evaluated in priority order but the host-work layer itself is optional (e.g. "Synthesis narrative (host boundary always reached, content optional)"), matching audit-goals.md and the executor's own doc comment.

options.label: Leave as-is, add one clarifying clause
options.answer: Keep the header text but add a one-clause parenthetical clarifying that "always runs" refers to the obligation always being reached/evaluated, not to host work always being produced.

evidence: spec/audit-workflow-design.md:366 header text "## Synthesis narrative (always runs)".
Body text two sentences later in the same section: "an explicit omitted result remains a defined terminal when the user declines that optional layer."

src/audit/orchestrator/obligationPolicy.ts synthesis_narrative_current arm (~line 287-308): narrativeEnabled:false takes the deterministic OMIT arm with zero host work emitted; no narrativeEnabled value HALTs at a host boundary instead.
src/audit/orchestrator/synthesisExecutors.ts (~line 143-146): executor doc comment calls this "the optional synthesis-narrative obligation".

spec/audit/audit-goals.md: "the optional host-authored synthesis narrative may add an additive themes layer... when configured; it never replaces, gates, or is required by the deterministic output" — no "always" framing.

Independent adversary lane caught this 2026-10-23; the reviewer lane's independent pass over the same file did not flag it, so this is reported as a single-lane finding with no refutation rather than a contested item.

items.subject: The checkout-staleness open-bugs.md entry carries dated, now-resolved illustrative numbers ("49 commits and several releases (through v0.55.13) behind origin/main... roughly 26 nights with no completed pass") ahead of its still-open Property ask
items.title: docs/backlog/open-bugs.md: trim the checkout-staleness entry's dated narrative, keeping only its still-open Property
items.eli5: One open-bugs.md entry asks for a real, still-missing mechanism: a check that stops the nightly routine from reviewing docs against a local checkout that is badly behind origin/main (because reviewing stale code could reintroduce something a later commit deliberately changed). That ask is still open and valid. But the entry also quotes the specific numbers from the night it was written ("49 commits... through v0.55.13... roughly 26 nights") as if they were still true. Tonight's check shows local main is now exactly level with origin/main (the very next night's commits fixed that specific gap) — so those illustrative numbers are stale narrative about an already-resolved instance, sitting in front of the still-open general request. This is the kind of accreted post-mortem narrative the doc-review rubric asks to be trimmed on every pass, not just at the file's size ceiling.
items.question: Should the checkout-staleness entry in docs/backlog/open-bugs.md be trimmed to drop the dated instance narrative ("49 commits... through v0.55.13... roughly 26 nights") and keep only the Property statement (the still-open mechanism request)?

options.label: Trim to the Property only
options.answer: Trim the entry: remove the dated commit-count/version narrative sentence and keep only the Property statement describing the still-missing staleness-precondition check.

options.label: Keep as-is
options.answer: Leave the entry as currently written, including the dated illustrative numbers.

evidence: docs/backlog/open-bugs.md:13 quoted entry: "This run found local main 49 commits and several releases (through v0.55.13) behind origin/main on a clean tree, and the leg-1 scope ledger's newest coverage stamp was 2026-09-24 — roughly 26 nights with no completed pass on this checkout."

Verified tonight (2026-10-23): git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main = 0 and origin/main..HEAD = 0 — local main is now level with origin/main; the gap this narrative describes was closed by commits 1498feb8 and 49a5d1cd the following night.

The entry's own Property clause ("before leg 1 reviews a doc claim against code, the routine detects 'local HEAD has no unpushed commits and is behind its tracked remote' and treats that as a blocking precondition") names a mechanism that still does not exist — this half stays open regardless of the narrative trim.

items.subject: Three separate docs (docs/backlog/deferred.md, docs/backlog/open-bugs.md, docs/HANDOFF.md) each carry their own pointer to the same audit-refactor-qualification blocker, worded differently enough that it is unclear whether they describe the same blocked item or two distinct pieces of work
items.title: Doc-set condensation: three backlog/handoff homes point at the audit-refactor-qualification blocker — same item filed three times, or genuinely distinct?
items.eli5: There is one blocked piece of work: qualifying a reviewed audit-tools refactor candidate against a "serialized validation lane" before it can ship. Three different documents each describe this: docs/backlog/deferred.md calls it "awaits the serialized validation lane", docs/backlog/open-bugs.md calls it "still require[s] implementation and exact-tree qualification", and docs/HANDOFF.md names it as the immediate next step. Each is phrased differently enough that a reader cannot tell at a glance whether these are three views of the exact same blocked item, or two related-but-separate open questions (e.g. one about implementation work still needed, another about the qualification gate itself) that happen to cite the same background record. The doc-review rubric's corpus-level pass flags this as worth the owner's eyes — not because it is clearly duplicative (each is a pointer, not a restated copy, so it does not break the "one home per fact" rule in the letter), but because three backlog/handoff homes converging on one blocking condition is exactly the shape that pass exists to catch.
items.question: Are the deferred.md and open-bugs.md entries about the audit-refactor-qualification blocker the SAME blocked item filed under two different framings (implementation-work vs. qualification-lane), or genuinely distinct open items that happen to cite the same background record?

options.label: Same item — merge to one home
options.answer: They are the same blocked item described two ways; fold them into a single entry in one file (owner to pick deferred.md vs open-bugs.md) and delete the other.

options.label: Distinct — keep both, cross-reference
options.answer: They are genuinely distinct (one about pending implementation, one about the qualification gate); keep both but make each explicitly reference the other rather than let the overlap read as ambiguous.

evidence: docs/backlog/deferred.md:61 — "Audit refactor native qualification awaits the serialized validation lane. The qualification record separates accepted source patches from pending native gates, offline pipx/Lizard smoke and excluded work."

docs/backlog/open-bugs.md:58 — "Bounded audit refactors still require implementation and exact-tree qualification. Follow the finalized plan and qualification record; source review alone does not close the accepted defects or authorize release."
docs/HANDOFF.md:27-28 — "Next: qualify the isolated reviewed refactor candidate under the serialized validation lane; see the qualification record... for scope and remaining gates."

All three cite the same two background records (docs/reviews/audit-refactor-qualification-2026-10-14.md, docs/reviews/audit-final-refactor-plan.md). Flagged independently by the adversary lane 2026-10-23 as a low-confidence doc-set condensation observation; the reviewer lane did not raise it, so reported as a single-lane finding.

premise_probes.contains: Audit refactor native qualification awaits the serialized validation lane
Bounded audit refactors still require implementation and exact-tree qualification

items.subject: session-start-guards.mjs's stale-main-behind-origin check reads CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (the main checkout) instead of the session's own worktree, producing a false "BEHIND origin/main" warning inside a lap worktree that is actually level with origin
items.title: Leg-3 proposal P70: fix session-start-guards.mjs's stale-main check to read the session's own worktree, not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
items.eli5: When you work inside a git worktree (a second checkout linked to the same repo, used for a "lap" of work), the SessionStart hook that warns "you are behind origin/main, sync before writing code" was checking the MAIN checkout's git state, not the worktree you are actually sitting in. So a worktree that was perfectly up to date with origin/main still got the scary warning, because the separate main checkout happened to be stale. This exact bug (and an identical one in a different hook, the commit-time merge-routing check) was already logged as two separate backlog entries on two different dates (2026-10-06 and 2026-10-09), which is the nightly routine's bar for calling something a genuine recurring pattern rather than a one-off. Tonight's leg-3 pass wrote a ready-to-apply patch for the smaller of the two bugs: it adds a small helper that trusts the session's own working directory (the same pattern a few lines below in the same file already uses for a different check) and falls back to the old behavior whenever that information is not available, so nothing regresses for a session that is not in a worktree. A failing regression test was run against the unfixed code first (red), then against the patched code (green), and the existing test suite for this file still passes. The second bug (same root cause, in the commit-time merge-routing check) needs a different, larger fix and was deliberately left as a named follow-up rather than folded into tonight's patch.
items.question: Apply the P70 proposal (fix session-start-guards.mjs's stale-main check to read the session worktree instead of the main checkout) as written, and separately decide whether to also scope a fix for the related pre-commit-gate.mjs incomingPaths bug (2026-10-09, left out of this proposal as a materially different, larger change)?

options.label: Apply as-is
options.answer: Land the P70 patch (session-start-guards.mjs fix + regression test) as proposed; track the pre-commit-gate.mjs incomingPaths bug separately.

options.label: Apply, and also scope the pre-commit-gate.mjs follow-up now
options.answer: Land the P70 patch now, and additionally open a scoped task this lap to extend gitTargetDir's parsing to track a leading `cd` in a compound command, fixing the 2026-10-09 sibling bug.

options.label: Hold — needs more review
options.answer: Do not apply yet; the patch needs further review before landing.

evidence: docs/backlog/open-bugs.md (2026-10-06 entry): "The session-start 'commits BEHIND origin/main' warning measures the main checkout, not the session's worktree."

docs/backlog/open-bugs.md (2026-10-09 entry): "The merge-routing check measures incoming paths from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, not the checkout the command runs in." — same mechanism, different hook, left as a named follow-up.

Proposal, patch, and RED-AT.txt written to .audit-tools/nightly/proposals/P70-stale-main-reads-wrong-checkout/ (patch.diff, proposal.md, RED-AT.txt, and the new regression test tests/shared/hook-session-start-guards-stale-main-worktree.test.ts).

RED-AT.txt: regression test run against the unfixed hook at HEAD 49a5d1cd failed as predicted (verbatim failure quoted); same command passed (1 passed) once the fix was restored. Existing tests/shared/hook-session-start-guards.test.ts suite (11/11) unaffected.

items.title: 4-file uncommitted WIP has blocked leg-1's clean-tree gate for 2 nights — 3 of 4 edits verified correct, 1 is wrong
items.eli5: The working tree has carried the same uncommitted edits across four tracked docs (.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md, docs/backlog/forward-tracks.md, docs/backlog/minor-bugs.md, docs/glossary-ids.md) since at least 2026-10-23; last night's run found the tree dirty and, per the clean-tree rule, withheld its own new findings rather than layering on top. Tonight this run independently re-verified the pending edits against current HEAD, using AGY as an independent adversary from a throwaway worktree. Three of the four are confirmed correct: the ship/SKILL.md addition of the validate-source CI job, the INV-WTS path fix and INV-CDI-EXPLICIT-NODE-FIELDS row removal in glossary-ids.md, and both removed forward-tracks.md entries (production-orphan detection, now covered by durable memory; the ship-pipeline-stops-early entry, now shipped in release-and-publish.mjs). The fourth is wrong: the pending edit deletes a minor-bugs.md entry saying "the repo tool-input guard took a plain worktree sub-agent for an audit node" with the open property "the guard identifies an audit node from run state, not from the session's shape" — but .claude/hooks/tool-input-guard.mjs still classifies via a `dispatchShaped` regex over the prompt text (lines ~57-63), never run state, so the bug this entry describes is still live. Deleting the entry as-is would silently drop an unfixed bug from the backlog. Whether this WIP is the owner's own in-progress edit or an earlier interrupted nightly run's uncommitted output could not be determined from the tree alone.
items.question: How should the pending 4-file uncommitted WIP be resolved — commit the 3 verified-correct files and restore the wrongly-deleted minor-bugs.md entry, discard the whole WIP, or leave it for manual handling?

options.label: Commit the 3 correct files, restore the wrong deletion
options.answer: Commit .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md, docs/backlog/forward-tracks.md and docs/glossary-ids.md as-is (verified correct); restore the deleted tool-input-guard.mjs entry in docs/backlog/minor-bugs.md before committing that file, since the bug it describes is still live.

options.label: Discard all 4 pending edits
options.answer: Discard the pending WIP entirely across all 4 files; it was not an edit I intended to keep.

options.label: Leave as-is, I'll handle it
options.answer: Leave the working tree dirty; I will resolve the pending edits manually.
